solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Provide a report from inferior gallery, it’s said

indicators.note: something that is said is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: common means low-grade or inferior, and the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A critic is asked to write up a review of some second-rate art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, COMMON TATE runs together as COMMENTATE. The Tate is a group of national art galleries in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To commentate is to give a running spoken account of events, such as a sports match, which is delivering a report.

clue.text: Source of oil is too scented unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate state of affairs has gone wrong, so the letters come out badly arranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some perfumed oil turns out to be far too strongly scented for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of oil' could suggest a well or a field; here it is a crop product, and 'too scented' supplies exactly the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds of the cotton plant are pressed to yield an edible vegetable oil used in cooking and margarine.

clue.text: Rug is housemate’s in part

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word is wanted, a run of consecutive letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A flatmate claims a rug as partly their own property.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes 'housemate's' look like an owner, but it is just the word holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat is a small floor covering, essentially a little rug placed by a door or bed.

clue.text: One putting up with English clergyman

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates the company of an English vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up with' reads as tolerating, but 'with' is only the link; 'putting up' means building or raising.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is a person who raises or builds structures, so literally someone putting things up.

clue.text: Shred potato, adding in last bit of salt

indicators.note: the final bit of a word means just its closing letter
adding something in puts it inside, so one piece is inserted into the other

blocks.note: tater is informal for potato
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cook grates a potato and sprinkles in a pinch of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shred' looks like a kitchen verb here, but it is the noun definition. TATER is a folksy word for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatter is a torn strip or scrap of cloth or paper, the same thing as a shred.

clue.text: Force failing to open lock

indicators.note: a word that fails to open lacks its beginning, so its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: stress is a pressure or force acting on something

explanation.surface: Someone tries to force a lock but cannot get it open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long curl or strand of hair, which is what a lock of hair means.

clue.text: Initially coordinated hues, a mixture of coral and dark grey

indicators.note: at the start of each word, so only opening letters are used
a mixture blends things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decorator describes a colour scheme blending coral with dark grey.
explanation.walkthrough: The article 'a' is part of the letters being mixed, not just grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Charcoal is the name of a deep smoky shade of grey, taken from the burnt wood.

clue.text: Name the Spanish bird flying west

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means travelling right to left, backwards along the line

blocks.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to identify a Spanish bird as it heads westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish' means the Spanish word for 'the', a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name given to a book, film or piece of work, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Have trouble with gums? Here’s support article

blocks.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball
the definite article

explanation.surface: An advert for a product that helps people with sore gums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here's' reads the definition into the wordplay; the question mark flags the playful definition, which describes a baby rather than a dental patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies teething suffer sore, swollen gums as their first teeth push through, so a witty description.

clue.text: Fish I like lacking female’s vividness of colour

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: brill is a flatfish related to turbot
taken as written
to fancy something is to like it
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: An angler admires the bright colours of a fish, but not the female of the species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is a verb meaning fancy; remove the F of female to leave ANCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliancy is intense brightness or sparkle, and applied to colour means vivid, striking hue.

clue.text: Taro from the east? That’s not right for cereal plant

indicators.note: in an across entry, starting at the eastern end means travelling backwards along the line
not having something means leaving it out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether taro, an Asian root crop, counts as a cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: Taro is a starchy tropical root; turned around it gives ORAT, then the R goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a grass grown for their grain, which makes the oat a cereal crop.

clue.text: Staggered by Edward eating carnivorous animal

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
the otter is a meat-eating river mammal

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to see Edward feeding on a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggered' reads as amazed, but it means walked unsteadily.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily and sway, the same motion as staggering along.

clue.text: Rue arrest when changing financial officer

indicators.note: a thing that is changing takes a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company regrets the arrest that followed replacing its finance chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue' looks like a verb of regret, but it and 'arrest' are simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages the funds of a club, company or government, which is a finance role.

clue.text: Ridicule father embracing heartless aunt

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is removed, leaving only the outside letters
to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cruel dad mocks his sister while hugging her.
explanation.walkthrough: SIRE is a father, a word mostly used of horses and dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses mockery and irony to expose foolishness, so it is a form of ridicule.

clue.text: Sway from side to side on street walk

indicators.note: one thing on another follows it, so the first piece named is placed after the second

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a ship rolls when it sways from side to side

explanation.surface: A tipsy pedestrian lurches from side to side down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The swaying piece is placed after the street abbreviation to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely unhurried walk, so the two nouns share their meaning.

clue.text: Hydrocarbon is blue in general character, not black

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so a piece is placed within a longer one
not having something means it is excluded, so that letter is struck out

blocks.note: taken as written
the tone of something is its overall character or mood
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that some hydrocarbon has a bluish tinge overall, rather than black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' reads as a colour description, but it is the letters to insert; B for black is the pencil-grade convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Toluene is methylbenzene, an aromatic compound of carbon and hydrogen used as an industrial solvent.

clue.text: Current easy task

blocks.note: first meaning: a light movement of air
second meaning: something done without effort

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is a noun for moving air.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a gentle wind and, informally, a job so simple it takes no effort.

clue.text: Chosen exam about system of appointing MPs?

blocks.note: elect after a noun means chosen but not yet in office
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student picks an exam topic on how members of parliament are selected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' makes the definition adjectival: relating to the system. MPs are Members of Parliament in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral means relating to elections, the process by which voters choose Members of Parliament.

clue.text: Topic those people echo

blocks.note: them refers to those people
Echo is the radio alphabet code word for E

explanation.surface: People repeat the same subject over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echo' looks like a verb for repeating, but it is the radio-alphabet word for a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or central idea of a talk or piece of writing, so a synonym.

clue.text: Flower garland that is left to be sent back

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of the Latin id est, that is
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A garland of flowers left behind has to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but it is the one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn around the neck as a welcome.

clue.text: Bad cut with end of knife

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to sever is to cut through
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nasty wound made with the tip of a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad cut' reads as a single injury, but 'Bad' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe describes something serious or grave, as in a severe illness, so it matches bad in intensity.

clue.text: Delicate, small, of mini dimension ultimately

definitions.text: Delicate, small, of mini dimension ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the closing letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A description of something dainty and tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both defines the answer and, through the last letters of its first five words, spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf: small, slight and delicately built, matching the dainty tiny picture.

clue.text: That woman has left dad very overweight

indicators.note: someone who has left is gone, so those letters depart from the word

blocks.note: her refers to that woman
dad is short for father

explanation.surface: A woman walks out on her husband, who has grown very heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take HER out of FATHER and FAT remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat describes a body carrying a lot of excess weight, so someone very overweight.

clue.text: Cooked them evenly with great heat

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters are mixed into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe says to roast them evenly in a very hot oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With great heat' sounds like oven temperature, but it means with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat here is figurative, meaning intense feeling, so arguing with great heat is arguing passionately and forcefully.
